site.name: RCOS - Regenerative Community Operating System
site.description: RCOS is an open-source, shared system for organizing intentional communities. Clear, ready-to-use structures for decision-making, roles, resource sharing, and handling conflicts.

home.title: RCOS - Regenerative Community Operating System
home.hero.eyebrow: An open standard for intentional communities
home.hero.lead: Every community runs on rules, but most of them are never written down. Then a crisis forces the question, and the group has to decide in a hurry. RCOS collects those questions up front, so you can answer them calmly and together, before it hurts.
home.story.heading: The day nobody knew the rule
home.story.step1.title: Someone leaves
home.story.step1.body: A long-time member moves away. Everyone is sad, and in the middle of that grief a practical question comes up: what happens to their tools? Their room? Their share of the house they helped build? Nobody had ever decided.
home.story.step2.title: A decision in a hurry
home.story.step2.body: The group decides on the spot, under pressure and full of emotion. It's the best they can do in that moment, but not the choice they would have made with a clear head.
home.story.step3.title: The fallout
home.story.step3.body: Some people feel it was unfair. Old tensions come back. What started as grief turns into conflict, and it takes months to settle.
home.story.step4.title: The lesson
home.story.step4.body: Afterwards, the group sits down and writes a clear rule for next time: what belongs to whom, how leaving works, and who takes over which jobs.
home.story.step5.title: The real question
home.story.step5.body: Then someone asks the uncomfortable thing: what else have we never decided? Where is the next crisis we're not ready for?
home.story.punchline: RCOS exists to answer that last question.
home.what.heading: A list of the questions every community has to answer
home.what.body: RCOS, the Regenerative Community Operating System, is an open standard that collects the questions a community should settle before they turn into problems. It doesn't tell you what to answer. Your values, culture and choices stay yours. It makes sure you don't forget to ask.
home.what.examples_intro: In the standard, each question is written as a short, numbered rule, so everyone can point to it. Two examples:
home.what.example_exit.question: What happens to someone's things when they leave?
home.what.example_purpose.question: Why does this community exist, in one sentence that will still be true in ten years?
home.what.must_note: MUST means every community using RCOS has to give an answer here. The answer itself is up to you.
home.clause.2_1_1: A community MUST define exactly one primary purpose.
home.clause.3_6_1: Voluntary exit MUST be possible at all times.
home.clause.3_6_2: Exit procedures MUST be explicit, documented, and non-punitive.
home.clause.3_6_5: Asset, role, and responsibility separation MUST be defined prior to exit.
home.layers.heading: Seven layers, from “why we exist” to “how we change”
home.layers.body: The questions are sorted into seven layers. Each layer builds on the ones below it, and a higher layer can never overrule a lower one. That way, a day-to-day rule can't quietly undo your purpose.
home.layers.story_note: In the story above, the departure is a Layer 1 question, the fight is Layer 4, and writing a better rule afterwards is Layer 6.
home.layers.q0: Why do we exist, and what will we never do?
home.layers.q1: Who belongs, how do people join, and how do they leave?
home.layers.q3: How do money, land, tools and work flow?
home.layers.q4: What happens when things break between people?
home.layers.q5: How does the daily work actually get done?
home.layers.q6: How do we change our own rules without falling apart?
home.parts.heading: Five parts, each with one job
home.parts.body: You don't need all of them at once. Here is what each part is for.
home.parts.core.name: Core v0.1
home.parts.core.what: The standard itself: every rule, numbered and sorted into the seven layers.
home.parts.core.use: Use it when you need the exact wording, for example to check whether your community has covered everything.
home.parts.layers.name: Layers
home.parts.layers.what: Plain-language guides to each of the seven layers.
home.parts.layers.use: Start here if you want to understand the ideas before reading the formal rules.
home.parts.layers.example: Layer 4 explains how to handle conflict fairly, without blame games or quietly pushing people out.
home.parts.modules.name: Modules
home.parts.modules.what: Optional add-ons for topics not every community needs.
home.parts.modules.use: Pick the ones that fit what you do. Each adds its own questions on top of the core.
home.parts.modules.example: The Permaculture module adds rules for looking after land, water and soil over the long term.
home.parts.templates.name: Templates
home.parts.templates.what: Fill-in documents for every part of the core, in several file formats.
home.parts.templates.use: Use them to actually write your answers down, together, in a meeting.
home.parts.templates.example: The Exit & Separation Protocol: exactly the document the group in our story was missing.
home.parts.stress_tests.name: Stress tests
home.parts.stress_tests.what: Real situations where communities broke, replayed against RCOS.
home.parts.stress_tests.use: They show whether the rules hold up in real life, and help you spot warning signs in your own group.
home.parts.stress_tests.example: “Expulsion Without Due Process”: when a member can be pushed out with no process, no appeal and no record.
home.who.heading: Made for people who live and work together
home.who.founders.title: Groups starting a community
home.who.founders.body: Build the structure from day one, instead of patching it after the first crisis.
home.who.existing.title: Communities that already exist
home.who.existing.body: Find the questions you've never answered before they find you.
home.who.facilitators.title: Facilitators and mediators
home.who.facilitators.body: A shared, neutral language for hard conversations about power, money and conflict.
home.who.builders.title: Researchers and tool builders
home.who.builders.body: The whole standard is open and also published as structured data you can build on.
home.start.heading: Three small steps
home.start.step1.title: Get the big picture
home.start.step1.body: Read the seven layers in plain language.
home.start.step2.title: See where you stand
home.start.step2.body: Tick the warning signs that feel familiar, and see which stress tests your community is closest to.
home.start.step3.title: Write it down together
home.start.step3.body: Download the templates and start with Layer 0: your purpose. Everything else builds on it.

home.media.body: A short introduction video and a podcast episode about RCOS.
